title: Horizon and Orbit
premise: Rosalind Dunmore has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony network that stopped answering long ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers the 'forgotten' colonies were deliberately silenced — and the signal is a dying plea from survivors hiding in dead space. Pursued by the Consortium enforcers who engineered the silence, Rosalind races to reach an ancient relay at the edge of dead space to rebroadcast the truth before her vault's failing reactor detonates and erases both the evidence and her. She reaches the relay with minutes left, sends the archive wide, and chooses to stay behind as the vault burns — only for the survivors she saved to arrive in time to pull her from the fire, forging the found family that will carry humanity's seeds — and its conscience — outward again.
about_author: Casper Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural records before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep faith with forgotten things.

chapters.title: The Last Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She walks the seed vault's endless corridors, logging germination tests on crops no one will ever plant. Establishes her routines, her loneliness, and her stubborn tenderness toward living things. Emotional beat: devotion shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Silence on All Bands
chapters.summary: Rosalind reviews eleven years of unanswered transmissions to the colony network. A flashback shows the day the replies stopped. She almost accepts that everyone is gone. Emotional beat: the ache of talking into darkness.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The vault's array catches a fragmentary distress signal in Pre-Collapse Standard, a language extinct two centuries. Rosalind, one of few who can read it, realizes it is human, recent, and terrified. Emotional beat: electric hope curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Told Me
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The vault's aging reactor begins an unexplained countdown — someone triggered it remotely. She has roughly forty days before the vault and every seed burn. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Rosalind catalogs what she can carry: data cores, seed canisters, her grandfather's decoder ring. Interspersed memories of the family that built the vault and abandoned her to it. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and gift.

chapters.title: The Signal Speaks
chapters.summary: Decoding deepens: the signal names coordinates in dead space and repeats one phrase — 'they silenced us.' Rosalind understands the colony deaths were not accidents. Emotional beat: righteous anger igniting.

chapters.title: First Shadow
chapters.summary: A Consortium survey ship enters orbit, scanning the vault. Rosalind kills her lights and hides in the cryo-bay, listening to boots on metal above her. Emotional beat: hunted-animal terror.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Choice
chapters.summary: Rosalind could stay hidden and let the reactor kill the evidence quietly. Instead she loads a sledge with cores and seeds and sets out across the ice toward the old relay station at the edge of dead space. Emotional beat: courage chosen, not felt.

chapters.title: White Expanse
chapters.summary: Travel chapter. The frozen surface, a broken rover, a storm that nearly buries her. She talks aloud to the seeds to stay sane. Emotional beat: endurance and self-reckoning.

chapters.title: Waystation Nine
chapters.summary: Rosalind shelters in a derelict waystation and finds a stowaway: Juno, a feral teenage scavenger raised on derelicts, who tries to rob her and instead becomes her reluctant guide. Emotional beat: prickly first contact.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. She bargains passage for food and warmth, mocking Rosalind's mission but secretly hungry for purpose. First hint Juno's own family vanished in the silencings. Emotional beat: guarded longing for belonging.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the waystation's records, Rosalind finds shipping manifests proving the Consortium harvested colony populations for labor and erased the rest. Her decoded signal matches their pattern. Emotional beat: horror becoming clarity.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Consortium skimmers track them across the ice. A chase through crevasse fields; Juno's reckless flying saves them; the sledge of seeds is half-lost. Emotional beat: adrenaline and sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Juno Remembers
chapters.summary: By firelight, Juno admits her parents were 'relocated' when she was six; she survived by forgetting how to need anyone. Rosalind shares her own abandonment. Emotional beat: two orphans recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They sight the ancient relay — a cathedral of antennas standing in dead space's threshold, powered by a reactor older than the vault. But its keeper greets them with a drawn weapon. Emotional beat: awe undercut by threat.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Introduce Marek, ex-Consortium engineer who defected after wiring the silencing codes himself and has broadcast penance into the void for twenty years. He doesn't trust Rosalind's motives. Emotional beat: guilt meeting judgment.

chapters.title: Confession in the Antenna Field
chapters.summary: Marek reveals the countdown on Rosalind's reactor is his doing — an automated failsafe he built to destroy evidence if anyone came asking. He believes some truths get people killed. Emotional beat: betrayal and bitter understanding.

chapters.title: Three Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Rosalind argues the archive must go out anyway; Juno sides with her. Marek wavers. They have nineteen days before the vault detonates and before Consortium hunters triangulate the relay. Emotional beat: fragile alliance formed.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Living Language
chapters.summary: Quieter interlude: Rosalind teaches Juno to read Pre-Collapse Standard; Juno teaches Rosalind to laugh again. The relay hums around them like a heartbeat. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Coordinates
chapters.summary: Fully decoded, the signal resolves: thousands of colonists survived the purges, hiding in a hollowed moonlet in dead space, dying slowly without medicine or power. The relay is their only possible voice. Emotional beat: the stakes become faces, not abstractions.

chapters.title: Hunters Arrive
chapters.summary: A Consortium strike team lands at the relay's perimeter. Marek's old access codes buy hours, not safety. First blood is shed; Juno is grazed protecting the data cores. Emotional beat: the past turns violent.

chapters.title: Marek's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marek offers to surrender himself and confess on record if they let the others broadcast. Rosalind refuses to make him a martyr; Juno calls them both idiots. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against guilt.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: The team infiltrates the Consortium skimmer and cripples its pursuit capability, but Rosalind is captured covering their retreat. Emotional beat: sacrifice with a cliffhanger sting.

chapters.title: Inside the White Room
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, captive aboard the Consortium flagship. An interrogator, Director Voss, reveals the final cruelty: the vault's reactor countdown was never remote — it was always going to fail, and the Consortium simply let it. Emotional beat: despair interrogated and outlasted.

chapters.title: The Interrogator's Doubt
chapters.summary: Voss, herself a colony descendant fed sanitized history, begins questioning the ledger she enforces. Rosalind plants the seed: 'You silence us because you're afraid of what we remember.' Emotional beat: an enemy cracking open.

chapters.title: Escape Is a Team Sport
chapters.summary: Juno flies a stolen cutter into the flagship's hangar on a suicide-timed run; Marek overrides docking clamps from the relay. Rosalind walks out of captivity carrying Voss's private confession recording. Emotional beat: triumphant, breathless rescue.

chapters.title: Countdown: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Back at the relay, they learn the vault reactor accelerates — nine days now. Broadcasting to the hidden survivors requires physically aligning the great antenna, a weeks-long job. Emotional beat: arithmetic of hope.

chapters.title: The Alignment
chapters.summary: Montage-chapter: the three work the antenna gears by hand through storms and system failures, Juno in the crawlspace, Marek on the gantry, Rosalind calibrating. Emotional beat: communion through shared labor.

chapters.title: Voss Returns
chapters.summary: Director Voss arrives alone, off-record, demanding the full archive. Rosalind gives it freely — and asks her to stand aside when the fleet comes. Voss neither agrees nor refuses. Emotional beat: mercy offered to an enemy.

chapters.title: Signal to the Hollow Moon
chapters.summary: The relay fires. In dead space, the survivors' moonlet answers — thousands of voices, weak but alive, hearing a human language for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: catharsis; the loneliest woman on Earth is heard.

chapters.title: The Fleet Comes
chapters.summary: Consortium warships converge on the relay to erase everything. Marek readies the relay's one defensive trick: dumping its entire power reserve into a burst transmission that will also fry the station. Emotional beat: calm before annihilation.

chapters.title: Everything We Carried
chapters.summary: Rosalind must choose: save the physical seed canisters or stay to hand-align the final transmission vector manually. She sends Juno away with the seeds against the girl's screaming refusal. Emotional beat: heartbreak as inheritance passed on.

chapters.title: The Burst
chapters.summary: Climax part one. With warships firing, Rosalind and Marek hold the antenna true while the archive of the silencings floods every band in human space. The relay dies in light. Emotional beat: defiant transcendence.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Across the colonies, the broadcast lands: riots, resignations, Voss releasing the Consortium's internal records and turning state's witness. Justice arrives outside any courtroom. Emotional beat: the world changing in real time.

chapters.title: Ash and Seeds
chapters.summary: The vault detonates on schedule, unwatched. Rosalind, stranded at the dead relay with dwindling oxygen, records one last log — grateful, unafraid. Emotional beat: acceptance at the edge of death.

chapters.title: Ships in the Dark
chapters.summary: Out of dead space come the survivors' patched-together ships, guided by the broadcast, with Juno aboard leading them home. They find Rosalind alive by hours. Emotional beat: rescue as grace; the forgotten remembering each other.

chapters.title: New Orbit
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the survivor fleet orbits Earth, and the colonists ask Rosalind to lead the replanting — of crops, archives, and accountability tribunals. She hesitates, then says yes, with Juno and Marek beside her. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership accepted.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Rosalind plants the first restored seedbed in the vault's scorched outer greenhouse, Juno reading Pre-Collapse Standard aloud beside her. The dead language lives again because someone refused to stop listening. Emotional beat: renewal earned.

chapters.title: Orbit
chapters.summary: Final chapter, epilogue-style. Years on, the rebuilt network carries many voices; Rosalind logs one last entry — no longer to silence, but to family scattered among the stars. The vault is gone; the keeping continues. Emotional beat: peace, continuity, love outlasting ruin.
